newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Main Norilsk plant sees flat PGM output.
newsitem.headline: Main Norilsk plant sees flat PGM output.

text.p: Norilsk Nickel's main nickel smelter, which accounts for 30 percent of the Norilsk group's output of platinum group metals (PGM), plans flat PGM output this year, a top plant official said on Wednesday.
"We plan for platinum group metals production this year to be the same as it was last year," Sergei Yershov, head of the electrolysing section of the nickel plant, told Reuters.
He declined to provide figures, saying that they were a state secret.
Nickel plant PGM exports in 1997 would total 55.0 percent of output, up from 1996's 52.9 percent, company figures showed.
Yershov said the nickel plant's annual PGM production was 40 percent below 1989 levels, when its nickel output -- which defines Norilsk's PGM output levels -- peaked at 127,750 tonnes.
The nickel plant's director, Mikhail Steklov, repeating earlier forecasts, said the smelter's 1997 nickel production would be flat at 1996's 100,000 tonnes.
Yershov said that 85-90 percent of nickel output would be exported, compared to 1996's level of 85-86 percent.
"It's more advantageous for me to produce cobalt," Steklov said, forecasting 1997 cobalt production of 1,700 tonnes, up from 1996's 1,500 tonnes.
He said Norilsk had enough industrially-explored ores to support PGM output at unspecified levels until 2020. Lesser-explored ores could support output to 2040.
The nickel smelter's output has been rising steadily since 1993's low of 85,400 tonnes.
PGM output figures at Norilsk, one of the world's biggest metal producers, are a fiercely guarded state secret.
The nickel plant exported all of its PGM output in 1989, 48.1 percent in 1993, 52.4 percent in 1994 and 55.5 percent in 1995, according to company figures.
The nickel smelter is the main part of the Norilsk Mining and Metallurgical Complex, which has other units that also produce PGMs. The complex is owned by the RAO Norilsky Nikel 0#NKEL.RUO group.
The group produced a total of 177,185 tonnes of nickel in 1996 against 180,100 tonnes in 1995. Cobalt output last year was 3,151 tonnes.
